title: The Sum of a Magic Square of Squares Can’t be an Even-Power
text:
After looking at the results from the code. One can guess that there isn’t a 3x3 magic square of squares whose sum is a perfect square. At first this seemed very hard to prove, well that is until a fun fact about all 3 by 3 magic squares share That its sum is equal to 3 times the number in the center. With this simple fact a simple proof by contradiction would seem to work best, for we leverage the irrationality of the square root of 3.
But first, we’ll have to prove that the sum of any 3x3 magic square really is 3 times its center number


For any 3 by 3 magic square the sum is equal to 3 times its center value. This surprising is pretty simple to prove. First, an arbitrary 3x3 magic square: \[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
A & B & C \\ \hline
D & E & F \\ \hline
G & H & I
\end{array}
\]
Now because this is a magic square its elements, in each row, column, and diagonal, when summed adds to a single value. Let’s call this value S.
\[\begin{align*}
&\text{So, we have}\\
&A + B + C = S,\ D + E + F = S,\ G + H + I = S\ \text{for each row}\\
&A + D + G = S,\ B + E + H = S,\ C + F + I = S\ \text{for each column}\\
&A + E + I = S,\ C + E + G = S\ \text{for each diagonal}\\
\end{align*}\]
Now, take the four equations \[\begin{align*}
D + E + F = S \\ A + E + I = S \\ B + E + H = S \\ C + E + G = S
\end{align*}\]
Observe that \[\begin{align*}
4S &= (D + E + F) + (A + E + I) + (B + E + H) + (C + E + G)\\
&= D + E + F + A + E + I + B + E + H + C + E + G
\end{align*}\]
Suggestively rewrite the right most side and left most side, and collect like terms \[\begin{align*}
4S &= E + E + E + A + B + C + D + E + F + G + H + I\\
&= 3E + (A + B + C) + (D + E + F) + (G + H + I)
\end{align*}\]
Remember the three equations \(A + B + C = S,\ D + E + F = S,\ G + H + I = S\)
Simplify the previous expression with it, and collect like terms \[\begin{align*}
&4S = 3E + (A + B + C) + (D + E + F) + (G + H + I) = 3E + 3S\\
&\Longrightarrow\ 4S = 3E + 3S\\
&\therefore S = 3E
\end{align*}\]
Hence, it has been demonstrated that the sum for an arbitrary 3 by 3 magic square is 3 times its center value.



The proof for this fact is arguably simple. It will be a proof by contradiction leveraging the irrationality of the square root of 3.
So first a quick sidetrack: the irrationality of the square root of 3.


Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that \(\sqrt{3}\) is rational.
Then there are some natural numbers \(p\) and \(q\) such that \(\sqrt{3} = \frac{p}{q}\). Then, \[\begin{align*}
\sqrt{3} &= \frac{p}{q}\\
3 &= \frac{p^{2}}{q^{2}}\\
3q^{2} &= p^{2}\\
\end{align*}\] \(p^{2}\) is a natural number, since \(p\) is, and 3 is a prime.
Thus, by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, for \(p^{2}\) to be a multiple of 3
\(p\) must also be a multiple of 3. \[\begin{align*}
p &= 3n\\
3q^{2} &= p^{2}\\
\Rightarrow\ 3q^{2} &= 9n^{2}\\
q^{2} &= 3n^{2}\\
\end{align*}\] By the same reason as \(p\), \(q\) must also be a multiple of 3.
Thus, \[\begin{align*}
q &= 3m\\
\frac{p}{q} = &\frac{3n}{3m} = \frac{n}{m}
\end{align*}\] Therefore, if \(\sqrt{3}\) could be written as a rational number, then it could always be written as a rational number with strictly smaller parts ad infinitum. This seems fine, but this is actually not fine.
Remember that the set of natural numbers with the standard numeric ordering \(\leq\) is a well-ordered set, meaning that every non-empty subset contains a least element. This implies that no rational number can have its parts be a strictly descending chain at infinitum.
Thus, by way of contradiction, the \(\sqrt{3}\) can’t be rational.




Now back to magic square of squares.
Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that there is a magic square of squares whose sum, let it be \(S\), is a perfect square. \[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
A & B & C \\ \hline
D & E & F \\ \hline
G & H & I
\end{array}
\]
\(A = a^{2},\ B = b^{2},\ C = c^{2},\ D = d^{2},\ E = e^{2},\ F = f^{2},\ G = g^{2},\ H = h^{2},\ I = i^{2},\ S = s^{2}\)
For some natual number \(a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, s\)
Then, \[\begin{align*}
S &= 3E\ (\because \text{S is the sum of a magic square})\\
s^{2} &= 3e^{2}\\
\end{align*}\]
Dividing both sides by \(e^{2}\) we have
\[\begin{align*}
&\frac{s^{2}}{e^{2}} = 3\\
&\Rightarrow \left(\frac{s}{e}\right)^{2} = 3\\
&\Rightarrow \frac{s}{e} = \sqrt{3} \\
\end{align*}\]
For some natual number e, and s This, however, is impossible as it contradics the irrationality of \(\sqrt{3}\).
Thus, by way of contradiction, there are no magic square of squares whose sum is also a (perfect) square.

title: The Sum of a Magic Square of Squares Can’t be an Even-Power
text:
For All Even Powers
Again, suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that there is a magic square of squares whose sum, let it be \(S\), is a perfect even power. That is \[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
A & B & C \\ \hline
D & E & F \\ \hline
G & H & I
\end{array}
\]
\(A = a^{2},\ B = b^{2},\ C = c^{2},\ D = d^{2},\ E = e^{2},\ F = f^{2},\ G = g^{2},\ H = h^{2},\ I = i^{2},\ S = s^{2n}\)
For some natual number \(a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, s, n\)
Then, \[\begin{align*}
S &= 3E\ (\because \text{S is the sum of a magic square})\\
s^{2n} &= 3e^{2}\\
\end{align*}\]
Dividing both sides by \(e^{2}\) we have
\[\begin{align*}
&\frac{s^{2n}}{e^{2}} = 3\\
&\Rightarrow \frac{(s^{n})^{2}}{e^{2}} = 3\ (\because a^{bc} = (a^{b})^{c})\\
&\Rightarrow \left(\frac{s^{n}}{e}\right)^{2} = 3\\
&\Rightarrow \frac{s^{n}}{e} = \sqrt{3}\\
&\Rightarrow \frac{\sigma}{e} = \sqrt{3}\ (\text{where}\ \sigma := s^{n})
\end{align*}\]
As the natural numbers is closed under multiplication, \(\sigma = s^{n}\) must also be a natural number.
Thus, \(\frac{\sigma}{e} = \sqrt{3}\) for some natual number e, and \(\sigma\).
This, however, is impossible as it contradics the irrationality of \(\sqrt{3}\).
Thus, by way of contradiction, there are no magic square of squares whose sum is also a (perfect) even power.

title: The Sum of a Magic Square of Squares Can’t be an Even-Power
text:
For Odd Powers
A similar proof was thought of for all odd powers, but after further inspection the proof failed, thus, there isn’t one for all odd powers.
In fact, contrary to expectations any odd power can’t be disproven to be the sum only leverging the irrationality of \(\sqrt{3}\). There might be other ways of disproving specific odd powers of all odd powers all together.
Though, I haven’t, yet, been successful in finding them.

title: An Introduction to Magic Squares
text:
1.Magic Squares
A magic square is a square grid of usually positive natural numbers whose sums of the numbers in each row, column, and diagonals are the same.
Here are a few examples,



the famous one


\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
17 & 113 & 47 \\ \hline
89 & 59 & 29 \\ \hline
71 & 5 & 101
\end{array}
\]
This one is made of primes. It’s sum is 177
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
7 & 12 & 1 & 14 \\ \hline
2 & 13 & 8 & 11 \\ \hline
16 & 3 & 10 & 5 \\ \hline
9 & 6 & 15 & 4
\end{array}
\]
This one is 4 by 4 and sums to 34


2.Magic square of squares
A magic square is a magic square of square if the numbers in each cell can be squared and the resulting grid is also a magic square.
No 3 by 3 magic square of squares has been found, but other magic square of squares have been.
Here’s one found by Euler. Its sum is 8,515. \[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
68^{2} & 29^{2} & 41^{2} & 37^{2} \\ \hline
17^{2} & 31^{2} & 79^{2} & 32^{2} \\ \hline
59^{2} & 28^{2} & 23^{2} & 61^{2} \\ \hline
11^{2} & 77^{2} & 8^{2} & 49^{2}
\end{array}
\]

title: Rudimentary Code for Searching Magic Square of Squares
text:
The first attempt that one can think of is using computers to just get a magic square of squares.
Ignoring the fact that it has been done(and upto the trillions) to do so we’d need a program.
Since the program doesn’t need to be heavily optimized we’ll just write it in python.


This is a simple python code for finding magic square of squares. A naïve approach to be sure but spamming for loops works well enough.
The method used is to look for magic square of squares using the pythagorean quadruples. For Pythagorean quadruples can be parametrically generated with the following formula. \[a = (m²+n²-p²-q²),\ b = 2(mq+np),\ c = 2(nq-mp),\ d = m²+n²+p²+q²\]

from itertools import permutations as iperms, combinations
from collections import defaultdict
from math import isqrt


# 1. Parametric generation

def find_quadruples_parametric(d_max: int) -> dict[int, set[tuple]]:
    """
    Build  solutions[d] = { (a,b,c), ... }  where a²+b²+c² = d².

    Uses the parametric form:
        a = (m²+n²-p²-q²),  b = 2(mq+np),  c = 2(nq-mp)
        d =  m²+n²+p²+q²
    for m,n,p,q > 0, gcd(m,n,p,q)=1, (m+n+p+q) odd.
    Non-primitives are covered by multiples k*(a,b,c,d).
    """
    from math import gcd

    primitives: set[tuple] = set()
    param_max = int(d_max ** 0.5) + 2

    for m in range(1, param_max):
        for n in range(1, param_max):
            for p in range(1, param_max):
                for q in range(1, param_max):
                    d = m*m + n*n + p*p + q*q
                    if d > d_max:
                        break
                    if (m + n + p + q) % 2 == 0:
                        continue
                    if gcd(gcd(m, n), gcd(p, q)) != 1:
                        continue
                    a = abs(m*m + n*n - p*p - q*q)
                    b = 2 * (m*q + n*p)
                    c = 2 * abs(n*q - m*p)
                    if a == 0 or b == 0 or c == 0:
                        continue
                    primitives.add((*tuple(sorted((a, b, c))), d))

    solutions: dict[int, set[tuple]] = defaultdict(set)
    for (a, b, c, d) in primitives:
        k = 1
        while k * d <= d_max:
            solutions[k * d].add(tuple(sorted((k*a, k*b, k*c))))
            k += 1
    return dict(solutions)


# 2. Repetition finder

def analyze_repetitions(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> dict:
    """
    For each value that appears across the triples of this d, count
    how many triples it belongs to.  This tells us which positions
    in a magic square each value is eligible for.

    Returns
    -------
    dict with keys:
        freq              – {value: count}
        value_to_triples  – {value: set of triples containing it}
        center_candidates – values with freq >= 4  (needed for 8/8)
        corner_candidates – values with freq >= 3
        usable_values     – values with freq >= 2  (can appear in 6/8 grid)
        solo_values       – values with freq == 1  (useless for magic squares)
    """
    freq: dict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
    value_to_triples: dict[int, set] = defaultdict(set)

    for triple in triples:
        for v in triple:
            freq[v] += 1
            value_to_triples[v].add(triple)

    return {
        "freq":             dict(freq),
        "value_to_triples": dict(value_to_triples),
        "center_candidates": sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f >= 4),
        "corner_candidates": sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f >= 3),
        "usable_values":     sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f >= 2),
        "solo_values":       sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f == 1),
    }


# 3. Make grid

_LINES = [
    (0, 1, 2),  # row 0
    (3, 4, 5),  # row 1
    (6, 7, 8),  # row 2
    (0, 3, 6),  # col 0
    (1, 4, 7),  # col 1
    (2, 5, 8),  # col 2
    (0, 4, 8),  # diag ↘
    (2, 4, 6),  # diag ↗
]

_LINE_NAMES = [
    "row 0", "row 1", "row 2",
    "col 0", "col 1", "col 2",
    "diag ↘", "diag ↗",
]

def _valid_lines(flat: tuple, S: int) -> list[str]:
    return [
        _LINE_NAMES[i]
        for i, (p, q, r) in enumerate(_LINES)
        if flat[p]**2 + flat[q]**2 + flat[r]**2 == S
    ]

def _make_result(flat: tuple, S: int, d: int, note: str = "") -> dict:
    score = sum(
        1 for (p, q, r) in _LINES
        if flat[p]**2 + flat[q]**2 + flat[r]**2 == S
    )
    return {
        "grid":        [list(flat[0:3]), list(flat[3:6]), list(flat[6:9])],
        "flat":        flat,
        "score":       score,
        "valid_lines": _valid_lines(flat, S),
        "S":           S,
        "d":           d,
        "method":      note,
    }

def _is_perfect_square(n: int):
    if n <= 0:
        return None
    r = isqrt(n)
    return r if r * r == n else None


# 4. search for magic squares (8/8)

def find_magic_center_out(d: int, triples: set[tuple],
                          analysis: dict) -> dict | None:
    """
    Grid layout:
        a  b  c
        d  e  f   ← row 1  (e is center)
        g  h  i

    e appears in 4 lines:
        row 1  →  (d, e, f)
        col 1  →  (b, e, h)
        diag ↘ →  (a, e, i)
        diag ↗ →  (c, e, g)

    Once we assign 4 triples to these lines and choose orientations,
    all 9 values are fixed.  We then verify the 4 remaining lines:
        row 0: a²+b²+c² = S
        row 2: g²+h²+i² = S
        col 0: a²+d²+g² = S
        col 2: c²+f²+i² = S
    """
    S = d * d
    v2t = analysis["value_to_triples"]

    for e in analysis["center_candidates"]:
        e_triples = list(v2t[e])

        # Try every combination of 4 triples for the 4 center lines
        for combo in combinations(e_triples, 4):

            # Try every assignment of which triple goes to which line
            for row1_t, col1_t, d1_t, d2_t in iperms(combo):

                # Extract the two non-center values from each triple
                r1 = [v for v in row1_t if v != e]  # → [d_val, f]
                c1 = [v for v in col1_t if v != e]  # → [b, h]
                dg1 = [v for v in d1_t   if v != e]  # → [a, i]  (diag ↘)
                dg2 = [v for v in d2_t   if v != e]  # → [c, g]  (diag ↗)

                if len(r1) != 2 or len(c1) != 2 or len(dg1) != 2 or len(dg2) != 2:
                    continue

                # Try all 2^4 = 16 orientations
                for d_val, f in (r1, r1[::-1]):
                    for b, h in (c1, c1[::-1]):
                        for a, i in (dg1, dg1[::-1]):
                            for c_val, g in (dg2, dg2[::-1]):

                                # Check all 9 values are distinct
                                all9 = {a, b, c_val, d_val, e, f, g, h, i}
                                if len(all9) != 9:
                                    continue

                                # Check the 4 non-center lines
                                if a*a + b*b + c_val*c_val != S:
                                    continue
                                if g*g + h*h + i*i != S:
                                    continue
                                if a*a + d_val*d_val + g*g != S:
                                    continue
                                if c_val*c_val + f*f + i*i != S:
                                    continue

                                # All 8 lines valid!
                                flat = (a, b, c_val, d_val, e, f, g, h, i)
                                return _make_result(flat, S, d,
                                                    note=f"center-out (e={e})")

    return None


# 5. search for imperfect one

def find_magic_row_pair(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> dict | None:
    """
    Fix row0 and row1 as valid triples.  Row2 is determined by columns:
        g = sqrt(S - a² - d²),  h = sqrt(S - b² - e²),  i = sqrt(S - c² - f²)
    Row2 is automatically valid (3S - S - S = S).  Check diagonals.
    """
    S = d * d
    row_candidates = [perm for t in triples for perm in iperms(t)]

    best_score  = 0
    best_result = None

    for r0 in row_candidates:
        a, b, c = r0
        used0 = frozenset(r0)

        for r1 in row_candidates:
            dv, e, f = r1
            if frozenset(r1) & used0:
                continue

            g = _is_perfect_square(S - a*a - dv*dv)
            if g is None: continue
            h = _is_perfect_square(S - b*b - e*e)
            if h is None: continue
            i = _is_perfect_square(S - c*c - f*f)
            if i is None: continue

            if len({a, b, c, dv, e, f, g, h, i}) != 9:
                continue

            flat  = (a, b, c, dv, e, f, g, h, i)
            diag1 = (a*a + e*e + i*i == S)
            diag2 = (c*c + e*e + g*g == S)
            score = 6 + diag1 + diag2

            if score > best_score:
                best_score  = score
                best_result = _make_result(flat, S, d, note="row-pair")

            if best_score == 8:
                return best_result

    return best_result


# 6. Search & scoring

def find_best_magic_square(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> dict | None:
    """
    Run center-out first (if any center candidates exist), then fall back
    to row-pair.  Return the highest-scoring result found.
    """
    rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)

    result = None
    if rep["center_candidates"]:
        result = find_magic_center_out(d, triples, rep)

    if result and result["score"] == 8:
        return result   # perfect — done

    rp = find_magic_row_pair(d, triples)
    if rp and (result is None or rp["score"] > result["score"]):
        result = rp

    return result


def score_all(solutions: dict, min_triples: int = 3) -> list[dict]:
    results   = []
    candidates = {d: t for d, t in solutions.items() if len(t) >= min_triples}
    total     = len(candidates)

    for idx, (d, triples) in enumerate(sorted(candidates.items()), 1):
        rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)
        n_center = len(rep["center_candidates"])
        note = f"  [center candidates: {n_center}]" if n_center else ""
        R = len(triples) * 6
        print(f"  d={d:>4}  ({len(triples):>2} triples, R={R:>3},"
              f" pairs={R*R:>6}){note}  [{idx}/{total}]")
        result = find_best_magic_square(d, triples)
        if result:
            results.append(result)

    results.sort(key=lambda r: r["score"], reverse=True)
    return results


# 7. Find repetition

def print_repetition_report(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> None:
    """Print a detailed repetition analysis for a single d value."""
    rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)
    S   = d * d

    print(f"\n  d={d},  S=d²={S},  {len(triples)} triples")
    print("  Triples:")
    for t in sorted(triples):
        vals_in_t = [v for v in rep["freq"] if v in t]
        print(f"    {t}")

    print()
    print("  Value frequencies (how many triples contain each value):")
    by_freq = defaultdict(list)
    for v, f in sorted(rep["freq"].items()):
        by_freq[f].append(v)
    for f in sorted(by_freq, reverse=True):
        role = {4: "CENTER candidate", 3: "CORNER candidate",
                2: "EDGE candidate",   1: "unusable"}.get(f, f"freq {f}")
        print(f"    freq={f} [{role}]: {sorted(by_freq[f])}")

    if rep["center_candidates"]:
        print(f"\n  8/8 MAY be possible — center candidates: {rep['center_candidates']}")
    else:
        print("\n  8/8 impossible for this d (no value appears in 4+ triples)")


# 8. Print grids

def print_grid(result: dict) -> None:
    grid  = result["grid"]
    flat  = result["flat"]
    S     = result["S"]
    d     = result["d"]

    print(f"\n  d={d}  S=d²={S}  score={result['score']}/8"
          f"  method={result['method']}")
    print(f"  Valid: {result['valid_lines']}")

    print("\n  Values:")
    for row in grid:
        print("   ", "  ".join(f"{v:>5}" for v in row))
    print("  Squares:")
    for row in grid:
        print("   ", "  ".join(f"{v**2:>7}" for v in row))

    print("  Line check:")
    for name, (p, q, r) in zip(_LINE_NAMES, _LINES):
        total = flat[p]**2 + flat[q]**2 + flat[r]**2
        mark  = "OK" if total == S else "--"
        print(f"    [{mark}] {name:8}: {flat[p]:>3}²+{flat[q]:>3}²+{flat[r]:>3}² = {total}")


# 9. int main()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    D_MAX       = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 100
    MIN_TRIPLES = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3

    print("=" * 65)
    print("  Pythagorean Quadruples + Magic Square Solver")
    print(f"  d_max={D_MAX},  min_triples={MIN_TRIPLES}")
    print("=" * 65)

    solutions = find_quadruples_parametric(D_MAX)
    total     = sum(len(v) for v in solutions.values())
    print(f"\nDistinct d values : {len(solutions)}")
    print(f"Total triples     : {total}\n")

    # --- Triple count ranking ---
    print("Triple count ranking (top 10):")
    print("-" * 65)
    ranked = sorted(solutions.items(), key=lambda x: len(x[1]), reverse=True)[:10]
    for rank, (d, triples) in enumerate(ranked, 1):
        rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)
        centers = rep["center_candidates"]
        center_str = f"  centers: {centers}" if centers else "  no center candidates"
        print(f"  #{rank:>2}  d={d:>5}  S={d*d:>8}  {len(triples):>3} triples{center_str}")

    # --- Repetition analysis for candidates with the most triples ---
    top_d = sorted(solutions, key=lambda d: len(solutions[d]), reverse=True)[:5]
    print("\nRepetition analysis for top-5 most-triple d values:")
    print("-" * 65)
    for d in sorted(top_d):
        print_repetition_report(d, solutions[d])

    # --- Full search ---
    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print("  Full search (center-out first, row-pair fallback)")
    print("=" * 65)
    results = score_all(solutions, min_triples=MIN_TRIPLES)

    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print("  Top results")
    print("=" * 65)
    for r in results[:8]:
        print_grid(r)

    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print("  Score distribution")
    print("=" * 65)
    freq = defaultdict(int)
    for r in results:
        freq[r["score"]] += 1
    for s in sorted(freq, reverse=True):
        print(f"  {s}/8  {'#'*freq[s]}  ({freq[s]})")

title: Rudimentary Code for Searching Magic Square of Squares
text:
This is a simple python code for finding magic square of squares. A naïve approach to be sure but spamming for loops works well enough.
The method used is to look for magic square of squares using the pythagorean quadruples. For Pythagorean quadruples can be parametrically generated with the following formula. \[a = (m²+n²-p²-q²),\ b = 2(mq+np),\ c = 2(nq-mp),\ d = m²+n²+p²+q²\]

from itertools import permutations as iperms, combinations
from collections import defaultdict
from math import isqrt


# 1. Parametric generation

def find_quadruples_parametric(d_max: int) -> dict[int, set[tuple]]:
    """
    Build  solutions[d] = { (a,b,c), ... }  where a²+b²+c² = d².

    Uses the parametric form:
        a = (m²+n²-p²-q²),  b = 2(mq+np),  c = 2(nq-mp)
        d =  m²+n²+p²+q²
    for m,n,p,q > 0, gcd(m,n,p,q)=1, (m+n+p+q) odd.
    Non-primitives are covered by multiples k*(a,b,c,d).
    """
    from math import gcd

    primitives: set[tuple] = set()
    param_max = int(d_max ** 0.5) + 2

    for m in range(1, param_max):
        for n in range(1, param_max):
            for p in range(1, param_max):
                for q in range(1, param_max):
                    d = m*m + n*n + p*p + q*q
                    if d > d_max:
                        break
                    if (m + n + p + q) % 2 == 0:
                        continue
                    if gcd(gcd(m, n), gcd(p, q)) != 1:
                        continue
                    a = abs(m*m + n*n - p*p - q*q)
                    b = 2 * (m*q + n*p)
                    c = 2 * abs(n*q - m*p)
                    if a == 0 or b == 0 or c == 0:
                        continue
                    primitives.add((*tuple(sorted((a, b, c))), d))

    solutions: dict[int, set[tuple]] = defaultdict(set)
    for (a, b, c, d) in primitives:
        k = 1
        while k * d <= d_max:
            solutions[k * d].add(tuple(sorted((k*a, k*b, k*c))))
            k += 1
    return dict(solutions)


# 2. Repetition finder

def analyze_repetitions(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> dict:
    """
    For each value that appears across the triples of this d, count
    how many triples it belongs to.  This tells us which positions
    in a magic square each value is eligible for.

    Returns
    -------
    dict with keys:
        freq              – {value: count}
        value_to_triples  – {value: set of triples containing it}
        center_candidates – values with freq >= 4  (needed for 8/8)
        corner_candidates – values with freq >= 3
        usable_values     – values with freq >= 2  (can appear in 6/8 grid)
        solo_values       – values with freq == 1  (useless for magic squares)
    """
    freq: dict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
    value_to_triples: dict[int, set] = defaultdict(set)

    for triple in triples:
        for v in triple:
            freq[v] += 1
            value_to_triples[v].add(triple)

    return {
        "freq":             dict(freq),
        "value_to_triples": dict(value_to_triples),
        "center_candidates": sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f >= 4),
        "corner_candidates": sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f >= 3),
        "usable_values":     sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f >= 2),
        "solo_values":       sorted(v for v, f in freq.items() if f == 1),
    }


# 3. Make grid

_LINES = [
    (0, 1, 2),  # row 0
    (3, 4, 5),  # row 1
    (6, 7, 8),  # row 2
    (0, 3, 6),  # col 0
    (1, 4, 7),  # col 1
    (2, 5, 8),  # col 2
    (0, 4, 8),  # diag ↘
    (2, 4, 6),  # diag ↗
]

_LINE_NAMES = [
    "row 0", "row 1", "row 2",
    "col 0", "col 1", "col 2",
    "diag ↘", "diag ↗",
]

def _valid_lines(flat: tuple, S: int) -> list[str]:
    return [
        _LINE_NAMES[i]
        for i, (p, q, r) in enumerate(_LINES)
        if flat[p]**2 + flat[q]**2 + flat[r]**2 == S
    ]

def _make_result(flat: tuple, S: int, d: int, note: str = "") -> dict:
    score = sum(
        1 for (p, q, r) in _LINES
        if flat[p]**2 + flat[q]**2 + flat[r]**2 == S
    )
    return {
        "grid":        [list(flat[0:3]), list(flat[3:6]), list(flat[6:9])],
        "flat":        flat,
        "score":       score,
        "valid_lines": _valid_lines(flat, S),
        "S":           S,
        "d":           d,
        "method":      note,
    }

def _is_perfect_square(n: int):
    if n <= 0:
        return None
    r = isqrt(n)
    return r if r * r == n else None


# 4. search for magic squares (8/8)

def find_magic_center_out(d: int, triples: set[tuple],
                          analysis: dict) -> dict | None:
    """
    Grid layout:
        a  b  c
        d  e  f   ← row 1  (e is center)
        g  h  i

    e appears in 4 lines:
        row 1  →  (d, e, f)
        col 1  →  (b, e, h)
        diag ↘ →  (a, e, i)
        diag ↗ →  (c, e, g)

    Once we assign 4 triples to these lines and choose orientations,
    all 9 values are fixed.  We then verify the 4 remaining lines:
        row 0: a²+b²+c² = S
        row 2: g²+h²+i² = S
        col 0: a²+d²+g² = S
        col 2: c²+f²+i² = S
    """
    S = d * d
    v2t = analysis["value_to_triples"]

    for e in analysis["center_candidates"]:
        e_triples = list(v2t[e])

        # Try every combination of 4 triples for the 4 center lines
        for combo in combinations(e_triples, 4):

            # Try every assignment of which triple goes to which line
            for row1_t, col1_t, d1_t, d2_t in iperms(combo):

                # Extract the two non-center values from each triple
                r1 = [v for v in row1_t if v != e]  # → [d_val, f]
                c1 = [v for v in col1_t if v != e]  # → [b, h]
                dg1 = [v for v in d1_t   if v != e]  # → [a, i]  (diag ↘)
                dg2 = [v for v in d2_t   if v != e]  # → [c, g]  (diag ↗)

                if len(r1) != 2 or len(c1) != 2 or len(dg1) != 2 or len(dg2) != 2:
                    continue

                # Try all 2^4 = 16 orientations
                for d_val, f in (r1, r1[::-1]):
                    for b, h in (c1, c1[::-1]):
                        for a, i in (dg1, dg1[::-1]):
                            for c_val, g in (dg2, dg2[::-1]):

                                # Check all 9 values are distinct
                                all9 = {a, b, c_val, d_val, e, f, g, h, i}
                                if len(all9) != 9:
                                    continue

                                # Check the 4 non-center lines
                                if a*a + b*b + c_val*c_val != S:
                                    continue
                                if g*g + h*h + i*i != S:
                                    continue
                                if a*a + d_val*d_val + g*g != S:
                                    continue
                                if c_val*c_val + f*f + i*i != S:
                                    continue

                                # All 8 lines valid!
                                flat = (a, b, c_val, d_val, e, f, g, h, i)
                                return _make_result(flat, S, d,
                                                    note=f"center-out (e={e})")

    return None


# 5. search for imperfect one

def find_magic_row_pair(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> dict | None:
    """
    Fix row0 and row1 as valid triples.  Row2 is determined by columns:
        g = sqrt(S - a² - d²),  h = sqrt(S - b² - e²),  i = sqrt(S - c² - f²)
    Row2 is automatically valid (3S - S - S = S).  Check diagonals.
    """
    S = d * d
    row_candidates = [perm for t in triples for perm in iperms(t)]

    best_score  = 0
    best_result = None

    for r0 in row_candidates:
        a, b, c = r0
        used0 = frozenset(r0)

        for r1 in row_candidates:
            dv, e, f = r1
            if frozenset(r1) & used0:
                continue

            g = _is_perfect_square(S - a*a - dv*dv)
            if g is None: continue
            h = _is_perfect_square(S - b*b - e*e)
            if h is None: continue
            i = _is_perfect_square(S - c*c - f*f)
            if i is None: continue

            if len({a, b, c, dv, e, f, g, h, i}) != 9:
                continue

            flat  = (a, b, c, dv, e, f, g, h, i)
            diag1 = (a*a + e*e + i*i == S)
            diag2 = (c*c + e*e + g*g == S)
            score = 6 + diag1 + diag2

            if score > best_score:
                best_score  = score
                best_result = _make_result(flat, S, d, note="row-pair")

            if best_score == 8:
                return best_result

    return best_result


# 6. Search & scoring

def find_best_magic_square(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> dict | None:
    """
    Run center-out first (if any center candidates exist), then fall back
    to row-pair.  Return the highest-scoring result found.
    """
    rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)

    result = None
    if rep["center_candidates"]:
        result = find_magic_center_out(d, triples, rep)

    if result and result["score"] == 8:
        return result   # perfect — done

    rp = find_magic_row_pair(d, triples)
    if rp and (result is None or rp["score"] > result["score"]):
        result = rp

    return result


def score_all(solutions: dict, min_triples: int = 3) -> list[dict]:
    results   = []
    candidates = {d: t for d, t in solutions.items() if len(t) >= min_triples}
    total     = len(candidates)

    for idx, (d, triples) in enumerate(sorted(candidates.items()), 1):
        rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)
        n_center = len(rep["center_candidates"])
        note = f"  [center candidates: {n_center}]" if n_center else ""
        R = len(triples) * 6
        print(f"  d={d:>4}  ({len(triples):>2} triples, R={R:>3},"
              f" pairs={R*R:>6}){note}  [{idx}/{total}]")
        result = find_best_magic_square(d, triples)
        if result:
            results.append(result)

    results.sort(key=lambda r: r["score"], reverse=True)
    return results


# 7. Find repetition

def print_repetition_report(d: int, triples: set[tuple]) -> None:
    """Print a detailed repetition analysis for a single d value."""
    rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)
    S   = d * d

    print(f"\n  d={d},  S=d²={S},  {len(triples)} triples")
    print("  Triples:")
    for t in sorted(triples):
        vals_in_t = [v for v in rep["freq"] if v in t]
        print(f"    {t}")

    print()
    print("  Value frequencies (how many triples contain each value):")
    by_freq = defaultdict(list)
    for v, f in sorted(rep["freq"].items()):
        by_freq[f].append(v)
    for f in sorted(by_freq, reverse=True):
        role = {4: "CENTER candidate", 3: "CORNER candidate",
                2: "EDGE candidate",   1: "unusable"}.get(f, f"freq {f}")
        print(f"    freq={f} [{role}]: {sorted(by_freq[f])}")

    if rep["center_candidates"]:
        print(f"\n  8/8 MAY be possible — center candidates: {rep['center_candidates']}")
    else:
        print("\n  8/8 impossible for this d (no value appears in 4+ triples)")


# 8. Print grids

def print_grid(result: dict) -> None:
    grid  = result["grid"]
    flat  = result["flat"]
    S     = result["S"]
    d     = result["d"]

    print(f"\n  d={d}  S=d²={S}  score={result['score']}/8"
          f"  method={result['method']}")
    print(f"  Valid: {result['valid_lines']}")

    print("\n  Values:")
    for row in grid:
        print("   ", "  ".join(f"{v:>5}" for v in row))
    print("  Squares:")
    for row in grid:
        print("   ", "  ".join(f"{v**2:>7}" for v in row))

    print("  Line check:")
    for name, (p, q, r) in zip(_LINE_NAMES, _LINES):
        total = flat[p]**2 + flat[q]**2 + flat[r]**2
        mark  = "OK" if total == S else "--"
        print(f"    [{mark}] {name:8}: {flat[p]:>3}²+{flat[q]:>3}²+{flat[r]:>3}² = {total}")


# 9. int main()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    D_MAX       = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 100
    MIN_TRIPLES = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3

    print("=" * 65)
    print("  Pythagorean Quadruples + Magic Square Solver")
    print(f"  d_max={D_MAX},  min_triples={MIN_TRIPLES}")
    print("=" * 65)

    solutions = find_quadruples_parametric(D_MAX)
    total     = sum(len(v) for v in solutions.values())
    print(f"\nDistinct d values : {len(solutions)}")
    print(f"Total triples     : {total}\n")

    # --- Triple count ranking ---
    print("Triple count ranking (top 10):")
    print("-" * 65)
    ranked = sorted(solutions.items(), key=lambda x: len(x[1]), reverse=True)[:10]
    for rank, (d, triples) in enumerate(ranked, 1):
        rep = analyze_repetitions(d, triples)
        centers = rep["center_candidates"]
        center_str = f"  centers: {centers}" if centers else "  no center candidates"
        print(f"  #{rank:>2}  d={d:>5}  S={d*d:>8}  {len(triples):>3} triples{center_str}")

    # --- Repetition analysis for candidates with the most triples ---
    top_d = sorted(solutions, key=lambda d: len(solutions[d]), reverse=True)[:5]
    print("\nRepetition analysis for top-5 most-triple d values:")
    print("-" * 65)
    for d in sorted(top_d):
        print_repetition_report(d, solutions[d])

    # --- Full search ---
    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print("  Full search (center-out first, row-pair fallback)")
    print("=" * 65)
    results = score_all(solutions, min_triples=MIN_TRIPLES)

    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print("  Top results")
    print("=" * 65)
    for r in results[:8]:
        print_grid(r)

    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print("  Score distribution")
    print("=" * 65)
    freq = defaultdict(int)
    for r in results:
        freq[r["score"]] += 1
    for s in sorted(freq, reverse=True):
        print(f"  {s}/8  {'#'*freq[s]}  ({freq[s]})")
